name: High Impact Professionals: support for people earning to give (Ambitious Impact, 2021 idea report)
summary: Ambitious Impact's 2021 estimate, made before launch, for a new charity supporting effective altruists who earn to give: community, mentoring and donor coordination so they give more and better. High Impact Professionals, incubated by Charity Entrepreneurship in 2021 for people in this group, was founded to run it; it has since moved toward helping professionals into high-impact careers (its talent directory and impact accelerator), so the estimate describes its starting plan rather than its work today. A re-implementation of AIM's spreadsheet, traced from its leverage ratio in the charity's third year (counterfactual donations raised per dollar spent, the average of three researchers' estimates); our bridge values the donations like the effective charities they go to. Ambitious Impact notes that 'this CEA is only comparable to other CEAs created for EA meta charities by Charity Entrepreneurship'.

source.title: EA Meta: Earning to give + (CE 2021 top idea report): CEA

sections.title: From donations raised to units of value (ours)
sections.explainer: charityevals' bridge, not Ambitious Impact's. Ambitious Impact counts value in counterfactual donations raised. That value reaches people through the charities the donations fund, so we value each such dollar like a dollar to GiveWell's top charities, in multiples of GiveWell's benchmark, with a wide range.

rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's headline for year 3, the average of three researchers' estimates (year 1: 3.5). The report: 'we would expect this organization to bring in significantly more than it spends, and this figure would increase over the first few years.' It counts only the 80% of the charity's value that comes through donations; better coordination and retention of people in the community are listed but not counted.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: A fundraising and community organisation: two co-founders' salaries are $100,000 of the sheet's $150,000 a year (Costs!B10:B13), so staff are most of the cost; the default for research and advocacy work (60%) is close. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

Share of the donations raised that wouldn't have gone to comparably effective charities anyway
rows.explainer: Used only with credit by share of resources on, where each contributor is credited with what its money adds. The micro and macro approaches count extra donations, but the ratio approach, which carries most of the year-3 estimate, uses other fundraising organisations' money moved per dollar (The Life You Can Save, REG, One for the World), which includes gifts their donors would have made to good charities anyway. Off, Ambitious Impact's counterfactual logic stands as published. Our judgment; the range is ours.

rows.label: Share of the outcome credited to the charity's cash budget
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, everyone who paid for the outcome shares it: the charity's budget, staff's forgone pay, and the donors whose gifts the charity raised (they pay for the good their gifts do). Off, this is 100%.

source.quote: This year, we expect to identify $400 million in 8x or better opportunities. (2021) / As of May 2026, our bar for funding programs is 6x our benchmark. (2026)

rows.explainer: The donations raised go where effective altruists earning to give donate. Ambitious Impact counts the value in 'equivalent donations to today's current top-tier EA charities', and warns that 'this CEA is only comparable to other CEAs created for EA meta charities by Charity Entrepreneurship'. To put such dollars on the site's scale we value them like donations to GiveWell's top charities at the time of Ambitious Impact's 2021 report: GiveWell then funded opportunities at '8x or better' its benchmark, so the best guess is 8 (its bar is 6 today). Low end 2: part of top-tier EA money goes to animal welfare and longtermist work, which has no agreed value on this scale, so we allow for these dollars being worth much less here than GiveWell's bar. High end 15: GiveWell's current model of the Against Malaria Foundation, as imported on this site, comes to about 0.049 units of value per dollar, 15 times the benchmark. The bridge and its range are ours, not Ambitious Impact's.
